institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I was very interrested in the nature and environment in Norway, due to the love I have for nature and that I'm studying biology, which is applicable when you're out exploring.
Also I am half Norwegian, so I wanted to explore the culture that I have always somewhat been seperated from.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good oportunity for self-exploring and development, meeting other cultures and people from all around the world. I've received many new friends. The teaching was quite a bit worse than in Denmark and on a lower level.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright, but sometimes it seemed like you required to do things that were actually not required. For example the "Proof of Attendance" document that was downloadable, was not required to be filled because we got a arrival and departure confirmation from our host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were some problems with my courses because you had to register, before summer (because of limited space), which was before we even had acces to the NTNU systems, so I couldn't join the courses that I wanted. And also some teachers had stopped prior to my arrival, so there were just fewer courses overall. These factors led to the availability of Biology courses in Autumn/winter, being very limited.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I used
Hybel.no
, and just posted that I was looking for an apartment. I did this 8 month prior to my exchange.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only know what my friends, that lived in student housing, told me, and I guess thats not relevant.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything happened very easily, most happened through the KU system. The last application date was may 1st. You needed to included different files with information: Passport, Learning Agreement, Course descriptions (courses you were going to take on NTNU), Courses taken in spring (back on KU), Erasmus Grant Agreement and an additional from with information about emergency contacts and such. Everything was quite easy with the process being described to you as you go.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write either NTNU exchange og KU exchange if you had any questions. But again sometimes it was hard to find their mail if you couldn't remember it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
As mentioned earlier, some classes required registering before we were even gived access to the NTNU systems, which was very annyoing, resulting in me having to choose 2 courses that I didn't find interresting or atleast not related to my bachelor.
Also a teacher (or more) had stopped just before I arrived which resulted in fewer courses to choose between overall.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect a lower level of teaching compared to KU, and also research if you have to write specifically to the teachers of a given course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As already mentioned, lower level compared to KU

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were lower compared to KU, but still alright, as you also had to take 4 course on the same time compared to "blok struktur" on KU Biologi atleast.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some things were the same: Some teachers were bright and you learned a lot, some were monotone and you received zero knowledge from their teaching. UCPH is better overall though, with the UCPH level being higher.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BI2043 - Biodiversity and Conservation Biology I
BI2034 - Community Ecology and Eco Systems
INTRO175 - Introduction to Norway
NEVR2030 - Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BI2034 - Community Ecology and Eco Systems.
It started off with a fun and interresting field trip to Dovrefjell, where you learned a lot and you got close with your colleagues.
And it was also the course I benefitted most from, as it was very relevant to my focus in biology: ecology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I hurt my shoulder so I had to pay for a physiotherapist (Luckily i had traveling insurance that covered it, so make sure you have that).
Different unplanned trips of experience(Trip to Lofoten, Surftrip and so on).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was a bit more expensive compared to Denmark, but not much. Also I think my housing was rather cheap compared to what my friends paid.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good sports system. Everything was either free or very cheap to participate in and also very available!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Almost any athletic activites you can think of.
ESN (Exchange student network) hosted several Cultural and social activites such as different trips around Norway, although I didn't participate.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Surf trip in Hoddevik with NTNUI Surf, mindblowing experience (Don't worry, you won't freeze), and its fun even as a beginner!
A trip to lofoten, one of the most beautiful places I've ever seen in my whole life. Can be arranged fairly cheap by yourself (a group of friends recommended), for around 3500,- DKK for housing, rental of cars and food. Then It will cost more if you want different experiences up there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on hiking trips both in summer, autumn and winter! The nature is breathtaking, but remember to bring som good hiking boots.
Surf trip, climbing (bouldering), Langrend and also Student samfundet is a big fun club for all students!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Norwegian culture is not far form the Danish, so it wasn't hard at all. Just a few language barriers and some things were done different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I was happy that KU gave us a list of other students going to the same destination, so you had someone to rely on in the beginning.
Also going on different sport trips organised by NTNUI or ESN trips can get you some friends!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think anything was that challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The friendships I made, and the experiences in the Norwegian nature, which has revitalized my love and interrest for Biology.
Also it was very fun to experience the Norwegian culture firsthand.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Contact the other students on the list that KU provides, so you have someone to hang with in the beginning at least.
Don't be afraid to try out new sports or try something that sounds crazy, its gonna be fun either way!
Save some money up or apply for different grants, so you don't have to worry about money while you're away.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the experiences in the beautiful nature of Norway. Also meeting Norwegians from different parts of Norway, so you learned the different dialects of Norway.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Reading up for the exam for nearly 2 months, because there are 4 at the same time compared to block structure in KU in Denmark. Also the limited amount of sun in Trondheim (4,5 hours when it topped), also made the exam reading extra hard.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
